summary_paragraph: A woman with HIV (off HAART, prior low CD4) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presented with several days of exertional shortness of breath and developed marked hypotension and presyncope after an extra dialysis session intended to remove additional fluid. In the ED she briefly required pressors and received a small fluid bolus with rapid stabilization; she received one empiric dose of vancomycin/piperacillin-tazobactam, but infectious evaluation including blood cultures was negative. Workup for dyspnea and cardiac causes showed no pulmonary embolism on CTA, no acute findings on chest radiograph, and a troponin rise felt to be stress-related with flat CK/CKMB and unchanged EKG. Echocardiography demonstrated an atrial septal defect/patent foramen ovale by bubble study and mild mitral regurgitation with preserved biventricular function and high-normal pulmonary pressures. Given elevated LDH with new thrombocytopenia and eosinophilia, evaluation for malignancy/lymphoma was initiated; abdominal ultrasound showed borderline splenomegaly without lymphadenopathy, and labs revealed elevated beta-2 microglobulin and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia. She continued her home M/W/F dialysis schedule with careful ultrafiltration, remained normotensive, and her shortness of breath resolved. She was discharged home with increased sevelamer dosing, continuation of cinacalcet and HIV prophylaxis (Bactrim and weekly azithromycin), and outpatient follow-up for HIV management, thrombocytopenia, immune protein abnormalities, and the echocardiogram findings.
problems: End stage renal disease on hemodialysis
Shortness of breath (resolved; unclear etiology, likely volume-related)
Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) disease, off HAART; on PCP/MAC prophylaxis
Elevated LDH with outpatient follow-up evaluation
Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia with elevated beta-2 microglobulin
Atrial septal defect/patent foramen ovale and mild mitral regurgitation on echocardiogram
History of herpes zoster with postherpetic neuralgia/chronic pain
